DecisionsDescription: What needs your decision. Everything is ticked: untick what you do not want, then approve.
NothingToDecide: Ahoy! Nothing needs a decision: the fleet is in good shape.
NoSourceConfigured: No source of findings is configured. Connect a Portarr, or point Orchestrarr at a sample file.
ShowingLastRead: Showing what was read at {time}. The last read failed: {error}
NoAutomaticPlan: Nothing can be done automatically here: a person has to act.
FindingFailingCi: The CI of the default branch is failing
FindingDependencyScanUnavailable: Dependency alerts are off or cannot be read: this repository is not known to be clean
StepMergePullRequests: Merge the pull requests that pass
ReasonNoPlacement: The environment description does not say where this runs.
ErrorFailed: The source could not be read
ErrorUnauthorized: The source refused the credentials, or asks to sign in
ErrorTimeout: The source did not answer in time
ErrorInvalidResponse: The source answered with something unexpected
MergeUnstable: Can be merged, a check that is not required fails
ForgeNotConnected: Not connected: pull requests are not read
ErrorRateLimited: The source asks to be read less often: its limit is reached
PullRequestsNotConnected: Pull requests were not read: no forge is connected.
PullRequestsFailed: Pull requests could not be read: {error}
PullRequestsStale: Showing the last list that was read.
PullRequestsNoneFound: The forge returned none of the {count} pull requests that Portarr counts. They may come from a bot that is not known here.
PullRequestsTruncated: Showing {shown} of the pull requests: there are more than the limit that is read.
PullRequestsCountMismatch: Portarr counts {count} pull requests, the forge returned {found}.
ApprovalStoppedHint: The global stop is engaged: nothing can be approved until it is released.
ApprovalNothingGrantedHint: No step of this plan is granted to Orchestrarr: grant one in the configuration (Powers) to approve it.
ApprovalWaitsHint: Approving makes a batch of tasks for the executor: it checks the code, its rights and the journal, then runs a dry run that starts nothing.
QueueDescription: The decisions you approved. Each one makes a batch of tasks that the executor checks and runs.
QueueEmpty: Nothing is waiting: approve a decision card and it appears here.
ActivityDescription: The audit trail: who decided what, what was refused and why, and the global stop. Newest first.
EventInstanceCreated: Database created: the global stop starts engaged
SignInFailed: Signing in failed. Try again; if it keeps failing, ask whoever runs this server.
StorageSqlite: Saved in a file: kept across restarts
StorageMemory: In memory: lost at every restart
KillSwitchEngaged: The global stop is engaged: nothing is approved and nothing launches.
KillSwitchFailed: The global stop could not be changed.
ApprovalErrorUnknownWorkItem: This decision is no longer there: refresh the list.
ApprovalErrorPullRequestsNotRead: The pull requests are not read yet, or only an old read is left: try again in a moment.
ApprovalErrorStepNotOffered: A ticked step is not possible here.
ApprovalErrorStepNotGranted: A ticked step is not granted to Orchestrarr.
ApprovalErrorStepNotSupported: A ticked step does not run yet.
ApprovalErrorMergeNeedsValidation: Merging needs the change to be built and tested first.
ApprovalErrorNoPullRequests: There is no pull request to approve.
ApprovalErrorAlreadyApproved: These pull requests were already approved at this commit.
ApprovalErrorTooManyRequests: Too many attempts: wait a minute and try again.
ApprovalErrorAuditUnavailable: The audit trail cannot be written or read, so the request is refused.
ApprovalErrorPlanChanged: The pull requests changed since you looked at them: read the card again, then approve.
ApprovalPullRequestsNotReadHint: The pull requests are not read yet, or only an old list is left: nothing can be approved on a list that is not read.
ApprovalNotOperatorHint: You are signed in but you are not an operator: you can read, and only an operator can approve.
KillSwitchOperatorsOnly: Only an operator can use the global stop.
KillSwitchCannotBeReleased: The global stop could not be released: its state cannot be saved, so it stays engaged.
KillSwitchCannotBeTraced: The global stop could not be released: the release cannot be written to the audit trail, so it stays engaged.
KillSwitchNotSaved: The global stop is engaged, but its state could not be saved or read: do not count on it across a restart.
SecondFactorHint: The 6-digit code of your authenticator app. The executor checks it; it is never kept.
ApprovalErrorTooManyPullRequests: This card holds too many pull requests for one batch: approve it after some are merged or closed.
ApprovalErrorSecondFactorRequired: Type the 6-digit code of your authenticator app.
RunsDescription: What the executor did with each approval: every check, every task, and the chained trace of what happened.
RunsEmpty: No run yet. Approve a decision and the executor will pick it up.
RunNoExecutor: No executor has taken it yet.
RunTraceChained: Each line carries the hash of the one before, the first the digest of the batch: a line changed or removed afterwards breaks the chain.
ApprovalStateDryRunDone: Dry run done: nothing was started
RefusalReplayed: this batch was already seen by the executor
RefusalSecondFactor: the code of the second factor was not accepted
RefusalKindNotAllowed: the executor does not accept this kind of task
RefusalRepositoryNotAllowed: the executor does not accept this repository
RefusalJournalMismatch: the batch is not the one that was approved (the journal does not hold it)
RefusalMalformed: the batch is not well formed
ExecutorNone: No executor has asked for work yet. Nothing runs until one does.
SecondFactorRequired: A code from your authenticator app, checked by the executor
QueueNoExecutor: No executor is connected: approvals wait until one asks for work.
SignInLocked: Too many failed attempts. Try again in a few minutes.
CannotReachServer: Orchestrarr cannot be reached. Reload the page in a moment.
IdentifierHint: This identifier is what your authenticator app is enrolled under: give it to the enrolment command of the executor.
PasswordChanged: Password changed. Your other sessions were ended.
PasswordRefused: This password is refused: it must be at least 12 characters and not the name of the account.
PasswordNotChanged: The password could not be changed.
AccountsDescription: Who can sign in, with which role. A change applies at once, and a disabled account loses its sessions.
AccountsNotAllowed: Accounts cannot be read: only an administrator manages them.
DeleteAccountConfirm: Delete the account {name}? Its sessions end at once.
AccountConflict: That name is taken, or the change would leave no administrator.
AccountInvalid: Refused: a name is 2 to 64 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores; a password is at least 12 characters.
EventLoginFailed: Sign-in refused: wrong name or password.
EventLoginLocked: Sign-in refused: the name is locked after too many failures.
EventPasswordLocked: Password check refused: too many failures.
EventAccountReset: Account reset with the break-glass password.
OptionsDescription: Switches for development and tests. Everyone reads them; an administrator changes them. What lowers security needs the host to allow it and your password.
OptionSecondFactorDescription: Approving a decision asks for the one-time code of your authenticator app, and the executor checks it. Turn it off only while developing or testing: with it off, a signed-in operator approves without the second proof.
OptionLockedHost: This host does not allow lowering security from the screen. It is started that way in production, and nothing here can change it.
OptionLockedConfiguration: The configuration of the host fixes this option: the screen cannot change it.
OptionTurnOffWarning: Without the code, anyone who is signed in as an operator can approve a decision with no second proof. The executor must be set not to ask for it either. The change is written in the activity trail.
SecondFactorOffBanner: The authenticator code is off: approvals carry no second proof. This is for development and tests.
ExecutorCodeMismatch: Approvals ask for a code but this executor does not check it, or the reverse.
